[agent-bulk] numucc_em, 21 showers, 27 segments. Verdict shower 1011 (pdg 11, kine_charge 135.8 MeV, 4 seg, len 22.6) -- correction 17: it is the only pdg==11 shower in scope and the highest kine_charge object; nothing higher was passed over. CORRECTION 6, READ THIS FIRST: this is a PID verdict and the event therefore carries NO clustering judgement. On clustering grounds alone I found nothing wrong -- the member set is one connected object, the only non-members within 20 cm are 29030 (1.6 MeV, 28.3 deg), 27028 (1.3 MeV, 55.0 deg) and 32033 (1.8 MeV, 61.2 deg), all sub-2 MeV single-segment showers well off the axis, and the 134.0 cm muon 1017 sits at dist 0.0 / angle 0.0 / tier 1 / metric 0 and is correctly NOT owned, so the shower did not swallow the muon stem. Membership triple-check agrees at 4 (nseg 4, owner-grouped candidates with owner==1011 are 1011/1012/1016/28029 = 4, cmp_div says 4 segment(s) plotted). VERTEX IS GOOD and I did not need to guess it: computing distances from the segment polylines in state.json, two segments start at exactly 0.0 cm from the main vertex -- 1017 (pdg 13, 134.0 cm) and 1015 (pdg 211, 28.2 cm) -- so the star sits on a real two-prong nu vertex. Judged from vtxz-az-055-el+20 (correction 20: vtxz-* were written automatically, event_half_span 165.0 cm, r95 132.0 cm) plus that arithmetic. Note the vtxz 60 cm frames show ONLY the vertex; shower 1011 is 129-137 cm away and is not in them. WHY THIS IS A PID VERDICT: 1011 is not shaped like an EM shower. Its two substantial members both radiate from the shower start and the angle between them is 164.5 deg, computed in 3-D from the member polylines (1012, 12.6 cm, direction (-1.9,-8.6,-7.2) from the start; 1016, 7.1 cm, direction (+0.7,+3.9,+5.6)). That is a straight ~19 cm line passing THROUGH its own start, not a cone opening from it, and shw1011-az+085-el+20 shows exactly that: a narrow straight streak with no cone, no branching and no widening, sitting on the endpoint of the 134 cm muon that arrives from the other side and passes within 1.9 cm of the start. START/AXIS WRONG (correction 9, phrase written verbatim so this can be grepped): the reco's start is in the MIDDLE of the object, and the orange axis arrow points along neither arm; there is no verdict string for that, so it is recorded here in the note. TWO READINGS I CANNOT SEPARATE, which is why the confidence is unclear: (a) it is not EM at all -- the 134 cm muon (range implies about 250 MeV KE, so it stops) ends here, and a stopping-muon endpoint gives either nuclear-capture fragments or a decay, which would look like short heavily-ionising prongs in opposing directions, exactly the 164.5 deg two-armed narrow object seen; (b) it IS a real electron and only the start is misplaced -- a 135 MeV electron travels about one radiation length (14 cm in argon) as a narrow MIP stem before showering, and this object is only about 19 cm long, so a genuine electron could legitimately look this narrow. What breaks the tie for (a) is that the charge extends on BOTH sides of the start (11.4 cm one way, 6.9 cm the other) and an electron leaves its origin in one direction only; what keeps (b) alive is that this is the same ambiguity the pilot recorded as unresolved on evt175896, and 135.8 MeV is too much for a Michel electron (53 MeV endpoint), which argues against the simplest version of (a). I did NOT compute MeV/cm from kine_charge/length (correction 18) and no PID conclusion here rests on a density number. Showers not looked at: the 20 skipped by the scope rule, all single-segment and 10.4 MeV or less. PI0: no reco group, pio_id -1, kine_div says no pi0 group in this event; the kine_pio_* line (mass 46.1, E2 10.4) is a BDT feature and not a pairing, and no pio-*.png was written. I propose no pairing. drag_check both true, probe_radius 123.3 px, probe_degenerate false.

[agent-bulk] numucc_em, 6 showers, 10 segments. Verdict shower 20004 (pdg 11, kine_charge 245.8 MeV, 2 seg, len 21.9). CORRECTION 17 MATTERS HERE: 20004 is only the SECOND entry of the kine_charge-ordered list, and it is the first with pdg==11. I passed over 20001 (pdg 13, kine_charge 251.3 / kine_best 342.9 MeV, a single 142.9 cm segment) which is the highest-energy object in the event, and 20002 (pdg 13, kine_charge 185.5 / kine_best 279.8 MeV, a single 113.4 cm segment). Both are long single-segment muon-like tracks, not EM showers, and I make no claim about either. VERTEX IS GOOD, and proven rather than eyeballed: computing from the segment polylines in state.json, THREE segments have a point at exactly 0.0 cm from the main vertex -- 20001 (142.9 cm), 20002 (113.4 cm) and 20004 (21.1 cm) itself. Judged from vtxz-az-055-el+20 (correction 20: vtxz-* written automatically, event_half_span 154.4 cm, r95 123.6 cm), which shows a clean three-prong star: blue 20001 up, green 20002 down-right, orange 20004 up-right. BOTH, and the two halves are not equally solid. OVER-CLUSTERED half (ROBUST -- it survives either PID reading below): 20004's second and only other member is 85013, a 0.74 cm pdg 2212 fragment at 73.7 cm / 25.0 deg, admitted by pass3_cone (direct). Its cmp_div reads distance 0.0-73.7 cm, angle 0.0-25.0 deg for just two segments, i.e. the member set is the shower body plus one speck three quarters of a metre away with nothing in between. On shw20004-az-055-el+20 that speck is a second, completely detached yellow halo sitting up beside the BLUE muon's charge, not on the orange body. On shw20004-acc.png it is the orange square sitting exactly on the corner where the 25 deg line meets the 80 cm line -- accepted at the extreme edge of the gate. UNDER-CLUSTERED half (CONDITIONAL): 20006 (pdg 13, 16.9 cm) sits at 17.6 cm / 4.76 deg from the shower start with metric 0.279, tier 1, and is the blue circle on the acceptance plot at (17.6, 4.8), DEEP INSIDE the innermost dashed box (5 deg out past 80 cm), yet it is excluded by in_main_cluster (walk_exclude). In the picture the grey 20006 continues almost exactly where the orange 20004 stops. So on one shower the gate rejected a candidate inside its innermost box and accepted one on the outermost corner. THE TWO READINGS I CANNOT SEPARATE, hence unclear: (a) 20004 really is an EM shower, and then 20006 is its own continuation and belongs -- both halves stand; (b) 20004 is NOT an EM shower at all but the first 21 cm of a third long track from the vertex -- the chain 20004 (21.1 cm) then 20006 (16.9 cm, 4.76 deg) then 20009 (101.2 cm, pdg 13, 30.7 cm out at 27.7 deg) reads in the picture as one roughly collinear track about 140 cm long, and an EM shower does not have a 100 cm straight tail. Under (b) the under-clustered half falls, the PID is what is wrong, and only the over-clustered half survives. Two things push toward (b): 20004 starts at 0.0 cm from the nu vertex, which a converted photon cannot do; and its blob point cloud is visibly fatter than the blue 20001 and green 20002 muon clouds in the same frame, i.e. it is more heavily ionising than a MIP, which suits a short hadron better than a 246 MeV electron. What pushes toward (a) is that a nue-like primary electron WOULD start on the vertex, and the event is only labelled numucc_em. I did NOT compute MeV/cm from kine_charge/length (correction 18); the ionisation remark above is a comparison of point-cloud density between three tracks in one frame, not a number. Correction 7, the marks differ in strength: 85013 OUT is the strong mark and is true under both readings; 20006 IN is the WEAK mark, conditional on reading (a), and is the one I would let the owner reverse. 20008 and 20009 are deliberately left unmarked at 31.7 and 27.7 deg. Showers not looked at: the 3 skipped by the scope rule (84012, 83011, 29010), all single-segment 2-point fragments. PI0: no reco group, all pio_id -1, kine_div says no pi0 group in this event and no pio-*.png was written; there is no second EM object, so I propose no pairing. drag_check both true, probe_radius 97.6 px, probe_degenerate false.

[agent-bulk] nuecc, 7 showers, 12 segments. Verdict shower 16014 (pdg 11, kine_charge 145.6, kine_best 102.2 MeV, 1 seg, len 35.5). CORRECTION 17: 16014 is the SECOND entry of the kine_charge-ordered list and the first with pdg==11. I passed over 16012 (pdg 13, kine_charge 275.1 / kine_best 382.4 MeV, 5 segments, 159.7 cm), the highest-energy object in the event; its own cmp_div is 0.0-143.1 cm at 0.0-10.4 deg, i.e. a long narrow chain, and I make no verdict on it -- but see the closing remark, because it bears on what this event is. CORRECTION 6, READ THIS FIRST: this is a PID verdict and the event therefore carries NO clustering judgement. On clustering grounds I found nothing wrong in either direction and want that on the record: 16014 has exactly one member (nseg 1, owner-grouped count 1, cmp_div says 1 segment(s) plotted at distance 0.0-0.0 cm, angle 0.0-0.0 deg -- the triple-check of correction 16 is trivially satisfied), so nothing foreign was swallowed; and every other segment in the event sits at 80.9-85.8 deg from its axis except 21015 (1.3 MeV, 34.1 cm out at 151.0 deg, i.e. behind the start) and 16012/16020 which touch it at the vertex, so there is no contiguous unclaimed charge anywhere in its cone to add. VERTEX IS GOOD and proven from the polylines, not eyeballed: three segments have a point at exactly 0.0 cm from the main vertex -- 16012 (23.8 cm, pdg 13), 16014 (35.5 cm) itself, and 16020 (1.9 cm, pdg 211, correctly unowned). Judged from vtxz-az-055-el+20 (correction 20: vtxz-* written automatically, event_half_span 180.2 cm, r95 144.2 cm), which shows a clean two-prong star with both prongs leaving the star itself. WHY THIS IS A PID VERDICT: on shw16014-az-055-el+20 the entire shower is ONE straight thin line running 35.5 cm from the vertex with a small hook at the far end -- no cone, no opening angle, no branching, and a blob point cloud whose width is indistinguishable from that of the neighbouring 16012 track in the same frame. 35.5 cm is about 2.5 radiation lengths in argon (X0 = 14 cm); a 146 MeV electron would have branched and widened well inside that, and this object does neither. The pilot's counter-argument on evt175896, that an electron starts as a narrow MIP stem for about one radiation length, does not rescue this one at 2.5 X0. Nor can this be a real electron whose shower charge was simply lost by clustering, because there IS no unclaimed charge downstream of its end to lose -- the five scope-skipped showers are 1.3 to 7.7 MeV fragments at 34 to 216 cm from the vertex, none of them in front of 16014. Supporting arithmetic, offered as corroboration only and NOT as the basis (correction 18): the usual trap does not bite here because 16014 is a single 60-point polyline that covers the whole object, so skeleton length is not under-covering blob extent. Converting to the track convention first with the display's own shower-to-track ratio (this event shows no such line, so I used the 154.2/256.3 = 0.60 printed on evt318769) gives roughly 87 MeV over 35.5 cm, about 2.5 MeV/cm, i.e. near MIP. That is consistent with the shape, and the verdict would stand without it. ONE THING FOR THE OWNER: this is labelled nuecc, and neither prong looks like an electron -- 16014 is a 35.5 cm MIP-like line and 16012 is a 159.7 cm narrow chain spanning 143 cm at under 10.4 deg, which is far too long for a 380 MeV EM shower (shower maximum is around 5 X0, some 70 cm). So the event may have no reconstructed EM shower at all rather than a mis-shaped one. I am not making that a verdict: 16012 is pdg 13 and out of scope for the verdict radio under correction 17. PI0: no reco group, both pio_id -1, kine_div says no pi0 group in this event and no pio-*.png was written; no pairing proposed. drag_check both true, probe_radius 87.6 px, probe_degenerate false.

There is nothing on-axis and unclaimed to add, so this is over-clustered only, not both. PI0: no reco group, all three in-scope pio_id are -1, and kine_div says no pi0 group in this event. The pio-*.png frames carry the capture's AUTO-slotted top two (38021 + 74055), which per correction 3 is NOT the reconstruction's pairing. Priced anyway: E1 136.2 + E2 53.0, axis convention 52.5 MeV, vertex convention 33.3 MeV -- both far below 135 and the two disagree by 1.6x. Combined with 38021 being attached to the vertex, I propose NO pairing and store none. 74055 (53.0 MeV, 4 seg, detached 21.5 cm from the vertex, cmp_div 0.0-51.7 cm at 0.0-7.4 deg) is the more photon-like of the two but has no plausible partner. [agent-bulk] nuecc, 5 showers, 6 segments -- the smallest event in my shard and a clean single-electron topology. Verdict shower 4000 (pdg 11, kine_charge 143.8 MeV, 2 seg, len 34.4); correction 17: it is the only pdg==11 shower in scope and the highest kine_charge object in the event, so nothing was passed over. VERTEX IS GOOD: 4000's own seed is the only segment with a point at 0.0 cm from the main vertex, and on vtx-az+065-el+20 the star sits exactly on the lower end of that segment. This is a single-prong vertex -- no hadronic recoil is reconstructed -- which is unremarkable for a quasi-elastic nuecc with a sub-threshold proton, and is not a vertex defect. NOTE THE FRAMING: event_half_span is 99.6 cm and r95 is 79.7 cm, both under the 150 cm threshold, so no vtxz-* frames were written; the vertex is judged off the ordinary vtx-* set. CORRECT, and the argument is about the non-members, not the shape (pilot section 2.3): every non-member in the event is either far outside the cone or behind the start. 30003 (pdg 2212, 4.3 MeV) is at 79.4 cm / 35.2 deg, 29002 (pdg 2212, 3.2 MeV) at 89.8 cm / 41.9 deg, 28001 (1.1 MeV) at 93.0 cm / 45.0 deg, and 31004 (1.2 MeV) at 31.4 cm / 120.1 deg, i.e. behind the shower start. There is nothing contiguous, on-axis and unclaimed anywhere to add. shw4000-acc.png makes the same point with no ambiguity at all: in the 0-40 cm by 0-15 deg window there are TWO orange squares, at (0,0) and (27.7, 2.6), and NOT A SINGLE blue circle -- nothing was rejected anywhere near this cone, so there is no just-outside-the-step case to argue about. Nothing foreign was swallowed either: the second member 47005 (14.8 cm, pass3_cone direct) sits at 27.7 cm / 2.6 deg, squarely on the axis, and cmp_div gives the whole member set as distance 0.0-27.7 cm at angle 0.0-2.6 deg. Membership triple-check per correction 16 agrees at 2 (nseg 2, owner-grouped candidates with owner==4000 are 4000 and 47005 = 2, cmp_div says 2 segment(s) plotted) -- worth stating explicitly on a 5-shower/6-segment event, where correction 16's usual trap is that nearly every segment is its own sub-20 MeV shower; here all four of those (30003, 29002, 31004, 28001, 1.1-4.3 MeV) are genuinely non-members and correctly left out. AND UNLIKE TWO OTHER EVENTS IN MY SHARD THIS ONE LOOKS LIKE AN EM SHOWER: on shw4000-az-055-el+20 the blob point cloud is diffuse and visibly WIDENS from the vertex outwards -- narrow around the first member and clearly fanned out around the second -- which is what a developing shower does and what the straight MIP-width objects I flagged on evt397401 and evt390634 did not do. So I have no PID doubt here and this verdict is a clustering verdict with nothing else attached. What correct means here is the pilot's fast-pass sense: nothing jumped out at the frames and the tables listed above, not a segment-by-segment verification. There is one small gap in the point cloud between the two members which I looked at and do not think is a defect, since 47005 is already claimed. Showers not looked at: the 4 skipped by the scope rule, which are exactly the four non-members named above. PI0: no reco group, pio_id -1, kine_div says no pi0 group in this event and no pio-*.png was written; there is no second EM object anywhere, so this is a single-electron event and no pairing is proposed. drag_check both true, probe_radius 70.7 px, probe_degenerate false.
